text:
If you are simply reinvesting the dividend (DRIP), why invest in SCHD? I can understand if you need the income and are spending the dividends (but that means NO DRIP). Investors that are young and thus their time horizon is long term, should invest in growth and concentrate on total return. I see too many youtubers and people that are young emphasizing dividend (and dividend growth) stocks or ETFs/mutual funds (like SCHD). Their justification is to build a portfolio of income/dividend producing stocks or ETFs/mutual funds. However, if they are simply reinvesting that income/dividends, it would be more advantageous to get a better overall total return. Then later on in life transform their portfolio to stocks or ETFs that produce income/dividends. Too much emphasis on high yield dividend stocks/ETFs/mutual funds at a young age will ultimately result in less overall wealth in the future. If you take a look at the time frame of SCHD's inception to yesterday's market close (as of 09/22/2026), here are their total returns (dividends reinvestment included) for a $10,000 investment: 
Growth of $10,000 10/20/2011 to 09/11/2026 (dividends reinvestment included) 
Thu 2011-10-20 to Tue 2026-09-22 
SCHD × 	$10,000.00 => $64,623.64
VOO × 	$10,000.00 => $83,487.06
QQQ × 	$10,000.00 => $150,350.20
FSELX × 	$10,000.00 => $450,904.03
SMH × 	$10,000.00 => $500,148.20
I used VOO, QQQ, FSELX and SMH for comparisons. Keep in mind, all of these pay dividends, but the payouts are small percentage-wise. The totals are drastically different since SCHD's inception date. The numbers, obviously, show that over that time period (since the inception of SCHD), all of these other ETFs/mutual funds are much better choices. But if you are a long term investor, ignore the volatility and just hold an investment that will give a superior total return over the long term. Of course, anything can happen in the future and in the market, so there are no guarantees.  Everyone is different and will have different viewpoints. I believe SCHD is a decent ETF, and if you need income right now, it may be a suitable investment. However, if I were young, it would not be my choice. When I was younger, I invested in VOO, QQQ as well as a small amounts in FSELX and SMH.  Since I am now retired, I transitioned some into SCHD for income.
